claims.text: StrongDM's factory charter states 'Code must not be written by humans' and 'Code must not be reviewed by humans'.
StrongDM's practical benchmark is that if a team has not spent at least $1,000 on tokens today per human engineer, its software factory has room for improvement.
Simon Willison notes the $1,000/day token figure amounts to about $20,000/month per engineer.
StrongDM defines a 'scenario' as an end-to-end user story often stored outside the codebase so coding agents cannot see it, making it holdout-like.
StrongDM replaced boolean green-test success with 'satisfaction', the fraction of observed trajectories through all scenarios that likely satisfy the user.
StrongDM's loop-completion principle is that the loop runs until the holdout scenarios pass and stay passing.
StrongDM's Digital Twin Universe clones Okta, Jira, Slack, Google Docs, Drive and Sheets.
In the Digital Twin Universe, agents build each twin as a self-contained Go binary from public API docs.
StrongDM's Attractor coding agent repo contains no code, only three markdown spec files.
StrongDM's CXDB stores conversation histories and tool outputs in an immutable DAG and comprises roughly 16k lines of Rust, 9.5k lines of Go and 6.7k lines of TypeScript.
Simon Willison flags the risk that coding agents write cheating tests, such as tests that simply assert true.
StrongDM's published techniques include Gene Transfusion, The Filesystem, Shift Work, Semport and Pyramid Summaries.
